Ⅱ. Eligibility 
 
Ⅲ. Nomination & Application Process 
 
GPA 
Requirement 
Hallym University does not have a specific minimum GPA requirement for incoming 
exchange students. However, it is essential that students meet the academic criteria 
established by their home institutions to be eligible for studying abroad. 
Language 
Requirement 
For courses taught in English, incoming exchange students are not obligated to 
provide evidence of their English language proficiency. However, their home 
institution must verify and confirm that the student possesses sufficient English 
language skills to attend lectures and complete coursework in English before 
nominating them to our university. 
 
For courses taught in Korean, there is no mandatory requirement for incoming 
exchange students to present proof of their Korean language proficiency. However, 
those who wish to enroll Korean language and culture-related classes designed for 
International Students (listed in the Courses link on page 3 of this factsheet) should 
have a beginner to intermediate level of Korean. For general courses taught in 
Korean, a TOPIK 2 or higher level of Korean is necessary to effectively participate. 
Nomination & 
Application 
Deadline 
Fall Semester 
 Nomination Deadline: May 1st 
 Application Deadline: May 15th 
Spring Semester 
 Nomination Deadline: November 1st 
 Application Deadline: November 15th 
Nomination 
Process 
The International Coordinator from partner universities can nominate applicants for the 
exchange student program using the designated Excel Form that we send via email 
during the nomination period.  
Application 
Process 
The nominated student, approved by the partner university, must complete and submit 
the application form along with the necessary supplementary documents within the 
specified application period. 
 
By default, all documents should be submitted online via email. However, students from 
non-OECD countries must also submit certain documents (refer to page 3) in hard copy 
via a traceable mail service such as FedEx, DHL, or EMS. These hard copy documents 
should be sent to the address provided on page 1 of this document. 
 
For documents submitted via email, students should send them to the exchange program 
coordinator at iao33@hallym.ac.kr.  
 
You can check whether your country is an OECD member by visiting below link. 
https://www.oecd.org/en/about/members-partners.html

Ⅴ. Visa Process 
 
Ⅵ. Academics 
Visa Documents 
Upon successful completion of the application process, the Hallym University 
coordinator will send the Certificate of Admission and other essential documents to 
both the applicant and the applicant's home university coordinator. These documents 
are required for obtaining a Korean visa. 
• Spring semester: Documents are sent in November. 
• Fall semester: Documents are sent in late May/early June. 
Visa Application 
Exchange students must obtain a D-2-6 visa from the Republic of Korea Embassy or 
Consulate in their home country before studying in Korea. This visa is mandatory, 
even if your country has a visa-waiver program with Korea for tourism or short-term 
stays. The specific documents required and application process (in-person or online) 
can vary depending on the embassy and your nationality. Therefore, it is essential to 
familiarize yourself with these details before applying.

Ⅶ. Life & Living 
Course Structure 
Most courses at Hallym University are worth 3 credits. A three-credit course consists 
of 45 hours of lectures spread over 15 weeks. Each week includes three hours of 
class, typically divided into two sessions. Some courses, however, have one three -
hour session per week. Additionally, there is one week dedicated to exams, making 
the total length of a semester 16 weeks.

Accommodation Exchange students are guaranteed 100% on -campus housing in one of the 
university's dormitories. 
Dormitory

- 2 students share 1 room (2 single beds) 
- Each room has a bathroom 
- Currently curfew 7 days a week.  
(Weekdays & weekends: 12am)

Dormitory 3 
- Price: KRW 724,000 per semester (Approx. USD 570) 
- 3 students share 1 room (3 single beds)

- You can live with Korean students who are proficient in foreign

Health Insurance 
• It is mandatory for international students with a D-2 visa to subscribe to the Korean 
National Health Insurance Service (NHIS).  The monthly insurance fee for 202 5 is 
KRW 76,390 (Approx. USD 53), but this may vary from year to year. 
• Hallym University strongly advises that you also obtain international travel and 
medical insurance for your exchange period in Korea. This insurance should cover 
the initial period of the semester before your NHIS becomes effective, as well as any 
travel outside of Korea during your exchange student program. 
• Even though you will be required to subscribe to NHIS after receiving your 
Residence Card  and paying the premium, it is still important to have additional 
international insurance. International insurance fills gaps in NHIS coverage, ensuring 
comprehensive care during your exchange.

 Dormitory fees do not include meal plans. Meals can be purchased at the University Cafeterias on 
campus. The cost of each meal ranges from USD 4 to 5. 
 The estimated budget for one semester is a guideline only. Actual costs may vary significantly 
depending on individual spending habits, travel frequency, and lifestyle. 
 The fees listed above are subject to change. 
  
Scholarships 
Available to 
Exchange Students 
Dormitory 3 Language Tutor Scholarship 
 
• Eligibility: This scholarship is open exclusively to students residing in Dormitory 3. 
Students from other dormitories are ineligible. 
• Selection Process: Applications and selections typically occur during the first week 
of each semes ter. The head professor of Dorm 3 conducts interviews and selects 
approximately 15 tutors. The exact number of tutors may vary per semester. 
• Scholarship Benefits: Successful tutors who complete their assigned duties will 
receive a full refund of their se mester dormitory fees.  Additionally, they will be 
awarded a rank -based scholarship ranging from approximately KRW 300,000 to 
KRW 600,000. 
• Please note that the scholarship amount and conditions are subject to change 
based on university policies. 
Buddy Program Exchange students are paired with Hallym University undergraduate students, 
known as buddies, who help them adjust to life in Korea and at the university. 
Programs for 
Exchange Students 
• Orientation: An orientation for exchange students is typica lly held on the Friday 
before the start of each semester and is mandatory. This event provides an 
opportunity to familiarize yourself with our international office staff, buddy student, 
and fellow exchange students. 
• Field Trip: A one-day field trip is organized for exchange and buddy students on a 
Saturday near the end of the first or beginning of the second month of each semester. 
Entrance fees to attractions, transportation costs, and other related expenses are 
covered. 
• Farewell Party: To conclude e ach semester, we host a farewell dinner where 
exchange students and their buddies can reminisce and bid each other farewell.

Ⅷ. Brief Information on Chuncheon  
 
"Chuncheon: A Captivating Blend of Nature, Culture, and Safety for International Students" 
 
Chuncheon(春川), the charming capital of Gangwon State and home to Hallym University, is a haven for 
international students seeking an unforgettable study abroad experience. Nestled amidst breathtaking 
natural landscapes and steeped in rich culture, this charming city offers a perfect balance of academic 
pursuits and adventure. 
 
• Nature's Playground: Surrounded by majestic mountains and the serene Soyang Lake, Chuncheon is an 
outdoor enthusiast's paradise. From hiking and boating to fishing and camping, there's always something to 
explore. 
 
• Cultural Tapestry: Immerse yourself in Korea's vibrant traditions through Chuncheon's diverse festivals 
and events. Experience the magic of the Chuncheon International Mime Festival, where world -renowned 
mime artists showcase their talents in a captivating blend of co medy, drama, and visual storytelling. Savor 
the local flavors at the Chuncheon Makguksu Dakgalbi Festival, a culinary extravaganza featuring the city's 
signature dishes: refreshing buckwheat noodles (makguksu) and spicy chicken stir-fry (dakgalbi). Cheer on 
talented athletes from around the globe at the World Taekwondo Cutural Festival, a showcase of the dynamic 
and graceful Korean martial art. Get your adrenaline pumping at the Chuncheon Marathon, also known as 
"The Legend of the Fall," one of Korea's thre e major marathons, offering stunning autumn scenery as you 
run. 
 
• A Foodie's Delight: Indulge your taste buds with Chuncheon's renowned cuisine. From spicy Dakgalbi 
(chicken and vegetable stir -fry) and refreshing Makguksu (buckwheat noodles) to the unique  flavors of 
freshwater raw fish, there's a dish to satisfy every palate. And with over 600 cafes, coffee lovers will be in 
heaven. 
 
• Safety and Comfort: Chuncheon is renowned for its safety and welcoming community. As part of South 
Korea, one of the world's safest countries, you can focus on your studies and enjoy your time without worry. 
 
• Legoland Adventure: Amusement park enthusiasts and LEGO fans alike will love Legoland Korea, Asia's 
largest Legoland and the world's second largest. Located in Chunche on, it's just a 15 -minute drive from 
campus. 
 
• Perfect Location & Affordable Living: Chuncheon is conveniently located within an hour's train or bus 
ride from the bustling city of Seoul. The overall cost of living in Chuncheon is lower compared to Seoul and 
other metropolitan areas, making it a more budget-friendly option for students. 
 
Experience the best of both worlds in Chuncheon: the tranquility of nature, the excitement of city life, and 
the warmth of Korean hospitality. Your adventure starts here! 
 
For more information, please visit Official Homepage of Chuncheon
